nodes.name: Schedule
nodes.notes:
What: Cron trigger that starts the analyst run once a day.
In: Fires on the cron expression 0 8 * * *, evaluated in the workflow timezone Africa/Cairo.
Out: One item carrying the trigger timestamp, which Init Run replaces with its own fields.
Why: Cron rather than a preset interval, so the hour is fixed instead of relative to activation.

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes:
What: HTTP entry point so the same run can be started by hand.
In: A POST to the path instabay-analyze.
Out: One item with the request headers, query and body, all of which Init Run ignores.
Why: responseMode is lastNode, so the caller gets Log Run's output back as the HTTP reply.

nodes.name: Init Run
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that stamps a run id and a start time for this execution.
In: One item from either the Schedule or the Webhook.
Out: One item with run_id set to wf4- plus the execution id, and started_at as an ISO timestamp.
Why: Run Stats reads both fields back at the end to build the audit row and compute duration_s.

nodes.name: Read Config
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Config tab of the Google Sheet, operation read.
In: The single item from Init Run. Sheet id 1idaFANX0dJtbl-ww6-Bca6WAFU6BUmwTon_wdxizXwk.
Out: One item per config row, each a key and a value.
Why: executeOnce, alwaysOutputData and one retry (maxTries 2), so an empty tab does not kill the run.

nodes.name: Read Calendar
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the Calendar tab of the same Google Sheet, operation read.
In: The config rows from Read Config, which it does not use because executeOnce is set.
Out: One item per calendar row, the post plan with status, format, pillar, slot and judge scores.
Why: Same executeOnce and one-retry pattern, and chaining after Config keeps both reads on one branch.

nodes.name: Select Published
nodes.notes:
What: Code node keeping only rows whose status is published and whose post_id matches b<n>-p<n>.
In: Calendar rows on the main input; both tabs are re-read by node name inside the code.
Out: One item per published post, the row plus follower_base, publish_mode, graph_api_version and token.
Why: It throws a named error when no row qualifies, and each config lookup falls back to a default.

nodes.name: Mode?
nodes.notes:
What: Switch that routes each post by the publish_mode value taken from Config.
In: One item per published post from Select Published.
Out: Output DryRun when publish_mode equals dry_run, output Live when it equals live.
Why: No fallback output is set, so a publish_mode that is neither value drops the post silently.

nodes.name: Engagement Simulator
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that simulates reach and engagement from followers, format, hour, pillar and caption.
In: One published post at a time, runOnceForEachItem, from the DryRun output of Mode?.
Out: A row with source synthetic: reach, likes, comments, saves, shares, video_views, engagement_total, er.
Why: The seed is an FNV hash of post_id fed to mulberry32, so the same post always gets the same numbers.

nodes.name: Get Insights
nodes.notes:
What: HTTP GET on the graph.facebook.com media insights endpoint for one post's metrics.
In: One post from the Live output of Mode?, supplying media_id, graph_api_version and ig_access_token.
Out: The Graph reply, a data list holding reach, likes, comments, saved, shares and views.
Why: media_id must already be on the Calendar row, and the token is sent in the query string.

nodes.name: Normalize Insights
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that reshapes the Graph reply into the simulator's row shape, mapping saved to saves.
In: One Graph reply at a time, plus the matching input item read back with $('Mode?').item.
Out: A row with source live, the same fields as the simulator, blank watch rate and an ISO measured_at.
Why: A helper returns 0 for any missing metric and ER falls back to 0 when reach is 0, so no NaN spreads.

nodes.name: Upsert Metrics
nodes.notes:
What: Writes each metrics row to the Metrics tab with appendOrUpdate, matching on post_id.
In: Metrics rows from either the simulator or the live normalizer, auto mapped from the item fields.
Out: The written rows, passed on to the aggregation step.
Why: Matching on post_id means a rerun overwrites each post's row instead of appending a new one.

nodes.name: Aggregate Stats
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that groups metrics by batch_id into means, breakdowns, post detail, top and bottom.
In: All metrics rows returned by Upsert Metrics.
Out: One item holding agg per batch, the batch list, latest_batch, next_batch and metrics_count.
Why: Each dimension is grouped twice, by ER and by absolute engagement, the agent's stated target.

nodes.name: Performance Analyst
nodes.notes:
What: AI agent that reads the batch aggregates and writes a short summary plus 3 to 5 directives.
In: The agg object as JSON text in the prompt, with latest_batch and next_batch named, labelled simulated.
Out: One item whose output field holds a summary string and a learnings array of directives.
Why: The system message sets the target metric and tells it to own and correct a past directive that hurt.

parameters.text:
=PER-BATCH ENGAGEMENT AGGREGATES (simulated engagement data for this exercise):
{{ JSON.stringify($json.agg) }}

LATEST BATCH: {{ $json.latest_batch }}. Your directives will steer batch {{ $json.next_batch }}.

Analyze and produce the learnings now. Output ONLY the JSON object.

options.systemMessage:
You are the Performance Analyst for Insta Bay's Instagram system. You write the verbal performance memory that steers the next content batch (Reflexion-style episodic memory).

You receive per-batch aggregates AND per-post detail rows (format, pillar, slot, reach, engagement, ER). The data is a simulated signal for this exercise - treat it as the ground truth to optimize against.

THE TARGET METRIC IS MEAN ENGAGEMENT ACTIONS PER POST (likes+comments+saves+shares). Slots and pillars mainly change REACH (audience size); formats change both reach and rate. So compare engagement_by_slot / engagement_by_pillar / engagement_by_format and the per-post rows - NOT engagement rate alone.

CAUSAL HYGIENE (critical, n is small):
- Beware confounding: a reel inflates whatever slot/pillar it sits in. When judging a slot or pillar, compare like-for-like (image posts vs image posts) using the per-post rows, or explicitly note the confound.
- Compare across batches when 2+ batches exist: if a slot/pillar was strong in one batch and weak in another, say why (what else changed?).
- If an earlier directive was applied and the metric DROPPED batch-over-batch, say so plainly, diagnose it in evidence, and issue a corrective directive.

Produce:
1. summary: 2-4 sentences - what worked, what did not, each claim backed by a specific number; if the previous batch's directives hurt the target metric, own it and explain.
2. learnings: exactly 3 to 5 directives for the NEXT batch, each on one of: format | slot | pillar | caption_style | hashtags.

Directive rules:
- Actionable by a copywriter: 'place the reel and 2 images in the 20:00 evening slot', not 'improve engagement'.
- Only reference pillars, formats, and slots that appear in the data.
- Respect the fixed weekly quota (exactly 1 reel + 1 carousel): direct WHERE to place formats, never to add more.
- Keep one slot or pillar as a comparison holdout, and say which.
- evidence: cite the numbers, e.g. 'image posts at evening-unwind averaged 39 actions vs 31 at late-morning'.

Output ONLY JSON: {"summary": "...", "learnings": [{"insight_type": "keep|stop|try", "dimension": "format|slot|pillar|caption_style|hashtags", "directive": "...", "evidence": "..."}]}

nodes.name: Analyst Model
nodes.notes:
What: OpenRouter chat model node running anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 at temperature 0.4 and 4000 max tokens.
In: Prompts from the two nodes it feeds, over the ai_languageModel connection.
Out: Model completions back to those nodes.
Why: It attaches to both Performance Analyst and Learnings Schema, whose autoFix needs a model of its own.

nodes.name: Learnings Schema
nodes.notes:
What: Structured output parser holding a manual JSON schema for a summary and a learnings array.
In: The raw model text from Performance Analyst, attached to it over the ai_outputParser connection.
Out: A parsed object where learnings is required and each item needs insight_type, dimension and directive.
Why: autoFix is on and evidence is left optional, so a missing citation cannot fail the whole run.

nodes.name: Emit Learnings Rows
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that turns the agent's learnings array into at most five rows; the summary is not saved.
In: The parsed agent output, plus latest_batch and next_batch read back from Aggregate Stats.
Out: Rows keyed b<next>-<dimension>-<n>, with batch_id, applied_in_batch, created_at and the agent fields.
Why: The id embeds the model's dimension word, so a rerun with new wording adds rows instead of updating.

nodes.name: Upsert Learnings
nodes.notes:
What: Writes the directive rows to the Learnings tab with appendOrUpdate, matching on learning_id.
In: Up to five learning rows from Emit Learnings Rows, auto mapped.
Out: The written rows, passed on to the RunLog read.
Why: Matching on learning_id means a rerun that rebuilds the same ids overwrites those rows in place.

nodes.name: Read RunLog
nodes.notes:
What: Reads the RunLog tab of the same Google Sheet, operation read.
In: The learning rows from the previous node, which it ignores because executeOnce is set.
Out: Every RunLog row in the tab, each carrying a workflow name, batch_id, duration_s and cost fields.
Why: Compute Benchmarks needs the WF2-content-studio rows to recover cost_per_post_usd and duration_s.

nodes.name: Compute Benchmarks
nodes.notes:
What: Code node computing brand, Arabic, lint, judge uplift, ER, engagement, reach, cost and latency scores.
In: Aggregates, calendar rows and run log rows, all pulled back by node name, looped over every batch.
Out: One row per metric per batch with benchmark_id, metric, value, unit and method, plus last-two deltas.
Why: The three simulator metrics carry a method text starting with SYNTHETIC, so nobody reads them as real.

nodes.name: Upsert Benchmarks
nodes.notes:
What: Writes the scoreboard rows to the Benchmarks tab with appendOrUpdate, matching on benchmark_id.
In: All benchmark rows from Compute Benchmarks, auto mapped.
Out: The written rows, passed on to the run stats step.
Why: Ids are rebuilt the same way each run, so the tab stays a fixed size instead of growing every day.

nodes.name: Run Stats
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds one audit row for this run, including the duration in seconds.
In: run_id and started_at from Init Run, plus latest_batch, metrics_count and batches from Aggregate Stats.
Out: run_id, workflow WF4-analyst, batch_id, started_at, finished_at, duration_s, posts_count and notes.
Why: llm_cost_usd and cost_per_post_usd are left empty, and the cost benchmark reads WF2 rows anyway.

nodes.name: Log Run
nodes.notes:
What: Appends the audit row to the RunLog tab, operation append.
In: The single run stats row, auto mapped from its fields.
Out: The appended row, which is also the HTTP reply body when the run came in through the webhook.
Why: Append, not the appendOrUpdate used by the other three writes, so each run leaves its own line.
